subject: Clarify DPA & transfer scope for AtlasEdge pilot
messages:
From: Sana Iqbal <sana@atlasedge.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasEdge Legal <legal@atlasedge.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:22:00 +0100
Subject: DPA scope for AtlasEdge pilot — SCCs/TIA ask

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the AtlasEdge engineering team is keen to start the 6-week pilot. Before we spin up test tenants, our legal/privacy team needs:

- Confirmation that Redwood can execute SCCs (controller-to-processor) and the standard DPA template for pilot data.
- A short Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) or confirmation that the pilot only processes EU-resident data and will remain in the EU.
- Clarification on roles: which party will be the data controller vs. processor for telemetry and support logs during the pilot.

We want to avoid a long review cycle; are you able to run a quick redline pass and tell us if there are any non-starters for AtlasEdge?

Attach: we can share our TIA draft if that helps.

Best,
Sana Iqbal
Head of Compliance, AtlasEdge
[Attachment: AtlasEdge_TIA.pdf (pdf, 120 KB)]

-----
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Sana Iqbal <sana@atlasedge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA scope for AtlasEdge pilot — SCCs/TIA ask

Hi Sana — thanks for the note and the clear asks. Looping in our legal and privacy leads (Laura, Monica) to do a focused review. Quick answers up front:

- We support the EU SCCs and typically sign a Redwood DPA that references SCCs for controller-to-processor transfers.
- For pilots, we can constrain processing to EU regions where customers request it; that will be an order-form item / deployment flag.
- For telemetry/support logs, we'll propose Redwood as processor, AtlasEdge as controller. If AtlasEdge needs certain support logs to be controller-owned, call that out and we can adjust.

Laura / Monica — can you confirm any DPA clauses that might be non-starters for a 6-week pilot and flag anything that requires engineering changes (e.g., data residency controls or redaction)?

Connor O'Brien
Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Sana Iqbal <sana@atlasedge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, AtlasEdge Legal <legal@atlasedge.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA scope for AtlasEdge pilot — SCCs/TIA ask

Hi all — I did a quick pass on the DPA scope and the AtlasEdge TIA you shared. Key points and ask list: 

1) SCCs: we can accept controller-to-processor SCCs. Our preferred approach is to append the SCCs and retain a short deviation log where we note role assignments. No legal blockers here.

2) TIA / transfer scope: the TIA shows that AtlasEdge will place pilot data in EU datacenters. We need a written confirmation from your side that the pilot tenant will not be replicated to non-EU regions and that backups are retained in-region for the pilot duration. If AtlasEdge cannot confirm, we will need to propose a supplemental Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA addendum) that documents additional safeguards (e.g., encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, contractual commitments on subprocessor locations).

3) Roles & telemetry: recommended language — Redwood is processor for logs/telemetry; AtlasEdge is controller. If AtlasEdge requires narrow processing as controller for specific support tasks, please list those operations explicitly (e.g., IP address mapping, user identifiers).

4) Limited liability / indemnities: AtlasEdge redlines around liability caps may require a short escalation to our legal director. For the pilot, we can accept a temporary carveout (timeboxed) but need to track that in the order form.

I've attached a redline (Redline_DPA_v2.docx) with inline comments. Key suggested edits are:
- Explicit in-region hosting clause for pilot: "Processing and backup of pilot data shall occur solely within the EU for the pilot period."
- Subprocessor list: allow only EU-based subprocessors for pilot (exceptions require written notice).
- Add TIA addendum template as an exhibit if replication outside EU is requested.

Please review the redline and let me know any critical business asks — we can aim for an exec sign-off if AtlasEdge confirms the in-region constraint.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redline_DPA_v2.docx (docx, 48 KB)]

-----
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@atlasedge.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Sana Iqbal <sana@atlasedge.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:55:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA scope for AtlasEdge pilot — SCCs/TIA ask

Thanks Laura — a few clarifications from AtlasEdge Legal: 

- We can confirm the pilot tenant will be deployed to our EU region (Frankfurt) and will not be replicated outside the EU for the pilot period. Backups are retained in-region.
- We need Redwood to confirm whether your monitoring/observability stack (prometheus/stackdriver equivalents) will ever pull logs to a US-hosted analytics account for operational reasons. If so, we need that excluded or listed as an exception with the protections you noted.
- Liability cap: for pilot PoC we can accept a temporary cap at 1x MRR but will escalate if full contract negotiation increases scope.

Can Laura / Connor confirm the monitoring question and whether the redline changes are acceptable for a pilot DocuSign? We are hoping to start the week of May 24.

Regards,
Rajiv
Legal Counsel, AtlasEdge

-----
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@atlasedge.com>, Sana Iqbal <sana@atlasedge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, AtlasEdge Legal <legal@atlasedge.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA scope for AtlasEdge pilot — SCCs/TIA ask

Rajiv / Sana — thanks for the confirmations and the timeline. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Monitoring/Observability: Redwood's operational monitoring is hosted in-region for pilot tenants by default; we will not pull pilot logs into US-hosted analytics accounts. If we need to engage a US-based SRE for an incident, that will be handled via a documented exception and only with your sign-off.
- Redline acceptance: Laura's suggested in-region clause and subprocessors constraint are fine for the pilot — we'll accept the redline in the attached doc and execute via DocuSign.
- Liability cap: we can proceed with the temporary 1x MRR cap for the PoC; legal teams to revisit at full contract stage.

Action items:
- Laura to upload final DPA to DocuSign (target: 5/18) — link will be sent to AtlasEdge legal.
- AtlasEdge to confirm pilot start week (target: 5/24).
- Connor to coordinate engineering flags to ensure EU-only deployment for the tenant.

I'll send the DocuSign link once Laura uploads. Thanks everyone — excited to get the pilot started.

Connor O'Brien
Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
[Related link: https://docusign.example.com/Env/1234-ATLASEDGE-DPA]
